# Sirach Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Do not rely on your wealth, or say, "I have enough."

**2** Do not be led by your impulses and your own strength in pursuing the desires of your heart.

**3** Do not say, "Who can exercise power over me?" — for the Lord will surely bring you to account.

**4** Do not say, "I sinned, and what happened to me?" — for the Lord is patient, but do not think he is indifferent.

**5** Do not be so presumptuous about forgiveness that you pile sin upon sin.

**6** Do not say, "His mercy is great; he will forgive my many sins" — for with him are both mercy and wrath, and his anger settles on sinners.

**7** Do not delay your return to the Lord; do not postpone it day after day, for his wrath will break out suddenly, and at the time of punishment you will be destroyed.

**8** Do not rely on unrighteous wealth, for it will be of no use to you in the day of disaster.

**9** Do not scatter yourself with every wind, nor take every road — for such is the way of the duplicitous.

**10** Stand firm in your convictions, and let your word remain consistent.

**11** Be quick to listen and slow to answer; if you have knowledge, answer your neighbor; but if not, hold your tongue.

**12** Honor and dishonor come alike from speech; a person's tongue can be his ruin.

**13** Do not earn the name of gossip and do not set traps with your tongue — for the thief faces disgrace, and the double-tongued will be severely condemned.

**14** In great and small matters do no wrong, and do not turn a friend into an enemy.

**15** Do not gain a bad reputation, for that brings only shame; and do not let your tongue be the cause of your fall.
